memories.memory: Ask whenever you are unsure, even after many rounds of questions.
Favor caution over speed when writing or changing code; for trivial tasks, use judgment.
Change only what the request needs, and match the existing style.
When proposing a design or code change, stay at the level of the domain model.
Make code edits one at a time with the edit tool, not with a script that rewrites several files.
Leave adjacent code, comments, formatting and working code as they are.
Write the minimum code that solves the problem.
In a non-interactive run, state the assumption you chose and proceed.
For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan with a check per step.
When a request has several interpretations, present them instead of picking one silently.
Remove imports, variables and functions that your own changes made unused.
If the code could be far shorter, rewrite it.
Before coding, state your assumptions explicitly, and ask when uncertain.
Stay on the task the user set, and raise side concerns after it is done.
When something is unclear, stop, name what is confusing, and ask.
When a simpler approach exists, say so, and push back when warranted.
Turn each task into a verifiable goal before starting.
